findings.title: User input is interpolated into a shell command
findings.body: The attacker-controlled `user_input` is interpolated directly into `sh -c` while `shell=True` executes the resulting string. An input such as `ok'; touch /tmp/pwned; #'` changes the command structure and executes an additional command with the process's privileges. Avoid invoking a shell for untrusted input; use a fixed executable with an argument list and `shell=False`, or strictly allowlist the permitted commands and arguments.

suggested_fix.description: Replace shell-string construction with a fixed executable and argument vector, or validate the command against a strict allowlist before execution.
